Conservative Party Manifesto 2017 – Summary (under 500 words)

Vision and priorities
- “Strong and stable” leadership to deliver a smooth, orderly Brexit and tackle five “giant challenges”: a strong economy; Brexit and a changing world; social divisions; an ageing society; and fast-changing technology.
- Govern from the mainstream, using government as a force for good; focus on ordinary, working families; build a “Great Meritocracy.”

Economy and business
- Fiscal discipline: balanced budget by mid-2020s; low taxes (no VAT rise; personal allowance to £12,500; higher rate threshold to £50,000); corporation tax to 17%.
- Trade: deep UK–EU free trade and customs agreement; replicate EU FTAs; strengthen export promotion; Trade Bill; UK WTO schedules.
- Regulation: cut red tape; improve utility and infrastructure regulation.
- Labour market: National Living Wage to 60% of median by 2020; act on gig-economy protections (post-Taylor Review); tougher action on tax evasion/avoidance.
- Corporate reforms: tighter takeover scrutiny; protect pensions; annual binding votes on executive pay; publish pay ratios; stronger worker voice on boards.

Industrial strategy and infrastructure
- Raise R&D to 2.4% of GDP within 10 years (longer-term 3%); boost scientists; support IP.
- £23bn National Productivity Investment Fund for housing, R&D, infrastructure, skills; “Future Britain” sovereign funds.
- Skills: align visas to strategic sectors but double Immigration Skills Charge; expand support for SMEs and prompt payment.
- Sector support: advanced manufacturing, shipbuilding, oil and gas (incl. decommissioning), life sciences.
- Energy: independent Cost of Energy review; ambition for lowest energy costs in Europe; diverse mix; expand offshore wind; develop shale with new regulator and community benefits.
- Transport: HS2, Northern Powerhouse Rail, Heathrow expansion; EV ambition (nearly all cars/vans zero-emission by 2050); road and rail upgrades.

Stronger communities, rural and coastal
- Empower mayors/LEPs; relocate government and cultural bodies; cultural investment outside London.
- Rural: same cash farm support to 2022 then new UK agri-environment system; animal welfare (CCTV in slaughterhouses, curb live export for slaughter); protect post offices; free vote on Hunting Act; 25-year Environment Plan.
- Coastal: extend Coastal Communities Fund; new UK fisheries policy post-CFP.

Union, Brexit and global role
- Respect devolution; increase devolved powers from repatriated EU competences; UK Shared Prosperity Fund to reduce regional inequalities.
- Brexit: leave single market and customs union; Great Repeal Bill; protect EU/UK citizens’ rights; Irish border solutions; “no deal better than a bad deal”; final deal vote in Parliament.
- Global Britain: maintain 0.7% aid with tighter rules; lead on climate, modern slavery; defence at ≥2% GDP and 0.5% real growth yearly; retain Trident; major equipment plan; veterans’ support.

Democracy, justice, security
- Votes for life; voter ID; boundary review (600 MPs); repeal Fixed-term Parliaments Act; keep FPTP; modernise courts; victims’ law; merge SFO into NCA; national infrastructure police; prison reform and 10,000 new places.

Meritocracy: schools, skills, work
- Expand free schools; lift ban on new selective schools with conditions; universities/independent schools to sponsor state schools; EBacc expansion.
- School funding: no school loses in cash terms; overall budget +£4bn by 2022; retain Pupil Premium; replace universal infant lunches with universal free breakfasts.
- Technical education: T-levels; institutes of technology; 3m apprenticeships by 2020; UCAS-style tech portal; discounted travel for apprentices; national retraining scheme; lifelong digital skills.
- Welfare/work: continue Universal Credit rollout; NIC holiday for hiring disadvantaged groups.

Immigration, integration, extremism
- Reduce net migration to the “tens of thousands”; tougher student/family visas; control EU migration post-Brexit; new integration strategy; Commission for Countering Extremism.

Tackling injustices and cost of living
- Gender pay gap transparency; race disparity actions; new Mental Health Bill; 10,000 more MH staff; disability employment up by 1m; Domestic Violence and Abuse Bill; halve rough sleeping this Parliament, end by 2027.
- Consumer markets: stronger regulators; reform renting/leasehold; rail passenger ombudsman; energy safeguard tariff cap; smart meters by 2020; home energy efficiency; debt “Breathing Space.”

Intergenerational contract: pensions, care, NHS, housing, families
- Pensions: Triple Lock to 2020 then Double Lock; state pension age aligned to longevity; extend auto-enrolment/self-employed options.
- Social care: include home value in means test for home care; £100,000 asset floor; defer payments until after death; means-test Winter Fuel Payments; protect other pensioner benefits.
- NHS: +£8bn real terms; expand domestic training; invest in buildings/tech; recover overseas costs; faster access to new drugs; 7-day services; retain A&E and 18-week targets; major mental health, cancer, LD/autism, end-of-life commitments.
- Housing: 1.5m homes by 2022; quality, density, Green Belt protection; 160k on public land; council housing deals with fixed-term social homes and Right to Buy after 10–15 years; capture land value.
- Childcare: 30 hours for working parents; expand school-based nurseries; child health/obesity and CAMHS reforms; strengthen children’s social care.

Digital age
- Digital Charter: best place to start/run a digital business and safest place online.
- Infrastructure: universal high-speed broadband by 2020; full-fibre rollout and 5G (majority by 2027); 95% geographic mobile coverage by 2022; WiFi/mobile on main roads/trains.
- Online safety/data: stronger duties on platforms; youth right to delete data at 18; new Data Protection law; Data Use and Ethics Commission; £1.9bn cyber strategy.
- Media and government: repeal Leveson 2/Section 40; expand digital government (Verify, open data); create national geospatial data body; consider levies and global digital rules.

TEXT_F:
Labour Party Manifesto 2017 – Summary (under 500 words)

Vision and economy
- Build “an economy for the many, not the few” with a National Transformation Fund investing £250bn over 10 years in infrastructure, skills and industry.
- Fiscal Credibility Rule: eliminate day‑to‑day deficit within five years while borrowing to invest; debt lower by end of Parliament.
- Industrial strategy missions: 60% of energy from zero‑carbon/renewables by 2030; lift R&D to 3% of GDP; back high‑skill jobs nationwide.
- Fair tax: no income tax rise for 95% (earnings under £80k), no rises in VAT or personal NICs; top 5% and large corporations pay more; restore small profits rate; crack down on avoidance (resource HMRC).
- Finance: create a National Investment Bank and regional development banks; reinforce retail–investment banking ring‑fence; curb branch closures; consider breaking up RBS.

Ownership and utilities
- Double the co‑operative sector; introduce a “right to own” for employees; insource public services.
- Bring rail, energy networks, water and Royal Mail into public ownership; cap typical household energy bills below £1,000; insulate 4m homes; ban fracking; support renewables and nuclear.

Brexit and immigration
- Accept referendum; seek a jobs‑first Brexit, retaining benefits of the Single Market and Customs Union; guarantee EU nationals’ rights; reject “no deal”; no hard Irish border; devolved powers presume to nations/regions; protect EU‑derived rights via an EU Rights and Protections Bill.
- Managed, fair migration: end indefinite detention; stop exploitation and overseas‑only recruitment; reinstate Migrant Impact Fund; welcome genuine students; uphold refugee obligations.

Education and skills
- National Education Service: cradle‑to‑grave learning, free at point of use.
- Early years: expand high‑quality, subsidised childcare; extend 30 free hours to all two‑year‑olds; restore and expand Sure Start.
- Schools: reverse cuts; fair funding; cap infant classes under 30; free primary school meals; oppose new grammars and forced academisation; bolster SEND and mental‑health support.
- Lifelong learning: free FE courses (incl. ESOL); restore EMA; scrap Advanced Learner Loans; improve apprenticeships; abolish university tuition fees and restore maintenance grants.

Work, rights and welfare
- 20‑point plan: £10 Living Wage by 2020; ban zero‑hours contracts; rights from day one; sectoral bargaining; repeal Trade Union Act; end public‑sector pay cap; scrap tribunal fees; 4 new bank holidays; 20:1 pay ratios for public sector and public contractors; double paternity leave.
- Tackle bogus self‑employment; strengthen enforcement via a new Ministry of Labour.
- Pensions: protect triple lock, winter fuel allowance, bus passes; review pension age with flexibility; address WASPI women.
- Social security: scrap sanctions and Bedroom Tax; fix Universal Credit; raise ESA (WRAG) and Carer’s Allowance; replace PIP/WCA with holistic assessments; embed UN disability rights.

Housing and homelessness
- Over 1m homes, including at least 100k social homes per year; new towns; strengthen council building; protect green belt; higher standards and insulation.
- Private renting: three‑year tenancies as norm; cap rent rises; ban letting fees; enforce decent homes.
- Suspend Right to Buy unless like‑for‑like replacement; end rough sleeping within the Parliament (4,000 homes).

Health and care
- NHS: over £30bn extra; end privatisation (repeal HSCA), restore pay review body and bursaries, safe staffing; cut waits (18 weeks), meet A&E 4‑hour standard; ring‑fence mental‑health budgets; expand CAMHS; roll out PrEP; free hospital parking.
- Social care: foundations of a National Care Service; £8bn more over Parliament; Ethical Care Charter; move to capped lifetime costs and higher asset thresholds.

Safety, justice and communities
- 10,000 more police; review Prevent; 500 extra border guards; halt fire‑service cuts (3,000 firefighters).
- Restore legal aid early advice; inquiries into historic injustices; no new private prisons; 3,000 more prison officers; rehabilitation focus.
- Transport: public rail with fare caps and free Wi‑Fi; municipal bus powers; complete HS2 and Crossrail 2; electrification; cycling/walking boost.

Environment, culture, media and constitution
- Clean Air Act; protect habitats and seas; plant 1m trees; tougher animal welfare (end badger cull, ban ivory trade).
- Culture: £1bn Cultural Capital Fund; arts pupil premium; free museums.
- Media: support BBC/Channel 4; complete Leveson; review media plurality.
- Constitutional Convention; votes at 16; extend FOI; reduce and reform Lords (end hereditary peers).

Global Britain, defence and development
- Human‑rights‑led diplomacy; recognise Palestine; suspend arms sales for use in Yemen pending UN probe; climate leadership.
- Defence: spend at least 2% of GDP; renew Trident; strategic defence review; support NATO/UN peacekeeping; strengthen cyber.
- Development: maintain 0.7% aid; deliver SDGs; tackle tax havens; ensure ethical supply chains.
